analysis: This PR adds a changelog fragment (changelog.d/reasoning-stop-outside-reasoning.md) and changes one table row in docs/architecture/inference.md (line 2126, outside the supplied base excerpt, which only shows lines 1-836). Both are documentation only. No code, key handling, attestation, authorization, encryption, billing or coordinator/provider protocol is modified. The documented behavior is that client `stop` sequences on Gemma 4 and `<think>` parsers match only `content`, excluding reasoning and tool-call spans (`ReasoningStopScope`). The native diffusion block engine carries no scope and matches the whole output. This is a functional/availability correctness change to stop matching. The implementing Swift sources (`ReasoningStopScope`, `EngineV2Bridge+StopSequence.swift`, `StopHoldback`) are not in the supplied batch, so I could not verify the behavior. Reviewing those would need to check that stop truncation cannot leak withheld reasoning or tool-call text into the returned content or the reported stop sequence. It would also check that the scope state does not persist across requests (the prompt-opened think-block start state). The docs claim per-request scoping. Threat-model relevance: T-008 (plaintext on failure) and T-041 (prefix cache) are not affected. A-001 handling is unchanged, and no threat-model update is needed from this docs change. No finding. The remaining open question is the unsupplied code that implements the documented behavior.
